overview: Asante architecture joined construction skill with visual language and religious practice. Surviving shrine buildings near Kumasi preserve parts of a tradition that remained meaningful beyond the period of imperial power.

items.text: Builders arranged timber and bamboo structures around courtyards, applying mud plaster to walls and originally roofing them with thatch.
Wall reliefs combine spirals with animal, bird and plant forms. Motifs related to Adinkra convey meanings as well as decorate surfaces.
Shrines are places for consultation with deities before important decisions. Their symbolic features belong to continuing religious practice.
Maintaining earthen buildings requires responding to heavy rain, humidity and damage to organic materials. Architectural survival depends on repeated care.
